'''Hermits''' are chewy [[Cookbook:Molasses|molasses]] [[Cookbook:Spices and herbs|spice]] [[Cookbook:Cookie|cookies]]. This version is on the strong side of the spectrum so those who prefer less hot-tasting food should hold back on the cloves and ginger.

==Ingredients==

*2 [[Cookbook:Cup|cups]] (275 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]]/9.7 [[Cookbook:Ounce|oz]]) [[Cookbook:All-purpose flour|all-purpose flour]]
*⅔ cup ({{convert|65|g|oz|abbr=on|disp=s}}) seedless [[Cookbook:Raisin|raisins]] (a handful more if you like them)
*⅔ cup ({{convert|120|g|oz|abbr=on|disp=s}}) packed dark [[Cookbook:Brown Sugar|brown sugar]]
*2½ [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|teaspoons]] ground [[Cookbook:Ginger|ginger]]
*2 teaspoons ground [[Cookbook:Cinnamon|cinnamon]]
*1 teaspoon ground [[Cookbook:Clove|cloves]]
*1 teaspoon [[Cookbook:Baking Powder|baking powder]]
*½ teaspoon [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]]
*½ cup ({{convert|175|g|oz|abbr=on|disp=s}}) molasses 
*6 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tablespoons]] [[Cookbook:Butter|butter]], melted
*2 teaspoons [[Cookbook:Vanilla|vanilla]] extract
*1 [[Cookbook:Egg|egg]]

==Procedure==

#Preheat [[Cookbook:Oven|oven]] to [[Cookbook:Oven temperatures|375°F/190°C]].
#Line a [[Cookbook:Baking Sheet|sheet pan]] with [[Cookbook:Parchment Paper|parchment paper]].
#In a large bowl, stir together flour, raisins, brown sugar, ginger, cinnamon, cloves, baking powder, and salt until well combined; watch the brown sugar to ensure that it doesn't clump—it will want to do so and brown sugar clumps coated in flour look a lot like raisins coated in flour.
#Stir in molasses, butter, vanilla, and egg until fully integrated. Shape the [[Cookbook:Dough|dough]] in two strips (approximately {{convert|6|x|3|in|cm|abbr=on|disp=s}}) separated by at least {{convert|1.5|in|cm|abbr=on}} on the sheet pan.
#[[Cookbook:Baking|Bake]] for 12–15 minutes, or until a [[Cookbook:Skewer|toothpick]] inserted into the center of the strips comes out dry.
#Allow to cool slightly then remove the hermits (on their parchment) to cooling racks to cool completely; be sure the bottoms have cooled (just reach under and feel—if its more than a little warmer than room temperature its not there yet). 
#Move the hermits (still on their parchment) to a counter for portioning and removal from parchment. Cut hermits into {{convert|1.5|in|cm|abbr=on}} wide strips (a [[Cookbook:Pizza Cutter|pizza cutter]] should work well) then carefully scrape them away from the parchment with a good thin [[Cookbook:Spatula|spatula]].
#Enjoy with a glass of [[Cookbook:Milk|milk]] or [[Cookbook:A Nice Cup of Tea|a nice cup of tea]].

== Notes, tips, and variations ==

* Although nice when warm these hermits will be even better after a night in an air-tight tin. They should last about a week.
* A buttered sheet pan works if you have no parchment, but it makes cooling and cutting more difficult and damaging to the sheet pan.

steps.text: Line a sheet pan with parchment paper.

In a large bowl, stir together flour, raisins, brown sugar, ginger, cinnamon, cloves, baking powder, and salt until well combined; watch the brown sugar to ensure that it doesn't clump—it will want to do so and brown sugar clumps coated in flour look a lot like raisins coated in flour.
Stir in molasses, butter, vanilla, and egg until fully integrated. Shape the dough in two strips (approximately ) separated by at least  on the sheet pan.
Bake for 12–15 minutes, or until a toothpick inserted into the center of the strips comes out dry.

Allow to cool slightly then remove the hermits (on their parchment) to cooling racks to cool completely; be sure the bottoms have cooled (just reach under and feel—if its more than a little warmer than room temperature its not there yet).

Move the hermits (still on their parchment) to a counter for portioning and removal from parchment. Cut hermits into  wide strips (a pizza cutter should work well) then carefully scrape them away from the parchment with a good thin spatula.
Enjoy with a glass of milk or a nice cup of tea.
